digest.component_or_area: reconciler transport typing and static type enforcement
propositions: Reconciler core modules pass transport parameters unannotated or as Any, preventing mypy from enforcing port completeness and catching missing members like set_entity_property that caused a357 to crash.

Importing TicketTransport through the unresolvable rebar_reconciler package shim causes mypy to widen the type to Any even when annotated, silently defeating static checks; relative imports resolve this.

Four capability members (add_comment, set_relationship, get_issuelinks_map, get_comment_map) carried by _TransportPortMeta metaclass are not visible to mypy for Protocol-typed values, causing false [attr-defined] errors at call sites unless narrowed to composed capability Protocols.

The _TransportPortMeta metaclass is load-bearing for runtime isinstance conformance checking and uncached member detection in assert_transport_conforms, but does not prevent mypy attribute-checking when the port type is resolvably imported.

Annotating transport parameters as the port type via relative imports and resolving all [attr-defined] gaps through capability narrowing or port declaration will enable mypy to catch a357-class defects at authoring time, complementing the runtime guard.
